1.text: Then Naomi her mother-in-law said to her, "My daughter, should I not seek a resting place for you, where it will be well with you?
1.amp: ...should I not seek rest [manoach -- a settled home and security] for you, that it may be well with you?
1.notes: manoach (H4494) = a place of rest/settledness -- the same 'rest' Naomi prayed for in 1:9. Once resigned to emptiness, she now actively seeks Ruth's good. The widow has become a matchmaker of grace.

2.text: Now is not Boaz, with whose young women you have been, our kinsman? Look — tonight he is winnowing barley on the threshing floor.
2.notes: Winnowing -- tossing the threshed grain into the evening breeze so the chaff blows away -- was done at night when the wind was steady. Naomi knows where Boaz will be, and the moment to act has come.

3.text: So wash yourself, anoint yourself, put on your cloak, and go down to the threshing floor; but do not make yourself known to the man until he has finished eating and drinking.
3.notes: Naomi sends Ruth as a bride prepared -- washed, perfumed, and robed. The widow's mourning is set aside for a bold, dignified appeal to the redeemer.

4.text: When he lies down, mark the place where he lies; then go, uncover his feet, and lie down. And he will tell you what to do."
4.notes: An act of humble petition, not seduction -- Ruth lies at his feet as a suppliant, putting herself under his protection and asking him, as redeemer, to act.

5.text: And Ruth answered her, "I will do everything you have told me."

6.text: So she went down to the threshing floor and did everything her mother-in-law had told her.

7.text: When Boaz had eaten and drunk and his heart was glad, he went to lie down at the end of the heap of grain. Then she came softly, uncovered his feet, and lay down.
7.notes: 'His heart was glad' marks contentment, not drunkenness. Ruth approaches quietly and waits -- the whole scene hushed and tense with hope.

8.text: In the middle of the night the man was startled; he turned over — and there was a woman lying at his feet!
8.amp: ...the man trembled [charad -- startled awake with a shudder] and turned himself, and behold, a woman lay at his feet.
8.notes: charad (H2729) = to tremble/start. The midnight surprise heightens the drama and Ruth's vulnerability -- everything now depends on the character of the man she has come to.

9.text: "Who are you?" he asked. And she answered, "I am Ruth, your servant. Spread the corner of your garment over your servant, for you are a kinsman-redeemer."
9.amp: ...spread your wing [kanaph -- the corner of your garment; the very 'wing' under which Boaz blessed her in 2:12] over your servant, for you are a redeemer [go'el].
9.notes: kanaph (H3671) deliberately echoes 2:12: Boaz prayed Ruth would find refuge under the LORD's wings; now Ruth asks Boaz to spread his own 'wing' over her -- to become the human answer to his own prayer. To 'spread the corner of the garment' was a marriage claim (cf. Ezek. 16:8). She is proposing redemption and marriage in one breath.

10.text: And he said, "May you be blessed by the LORD, my daughter. You have shown more lovingkindness now than at the first, by not going after the young men, whether poor or rich.
10.amp: You have shown more kindness [hesed -- loyal love] in the end than at the beginning, in not going after the young men.
10.notes: hesed (H2617) once more: Boaz reads Ruth's choice of an older redeemer over young suitors as a fresh act of covenant loyalty -- she seeks the dead husband's name and Naomi's good, not her own advantage.

11.text: Now, my daughter, do not be afraid. I will do for you all that you ask, for all my people in the town gate know that you are a worthy woman.
11.amp: ...for all the city of my people knows that you are a worthy woman [eshet chayil -- a woman of strength, valor, and noble character].
11.notes: eshet chayil (H802/H2428) = 'a woman of valor/excellence' -- the very phrase that crowns Proverbs 31:10. In the Hebrew canon Ruth stands beside Proverbs, so that the 'worthy woman' described there is shown living here. Note too the mirror: Boaz is a 'man of valor' (gibbor chayil, 2:1), Ruth a 'woman of valor' -- well matched.

12.text: Now it is true that I am a kinsman-redeemer; yet there is a redeemer nearer than I.
12.notes: A complication of honor: a nearer kinsman has the first right and duty to redeem. Boaz will not seize what is not yet his to take -- his integrity will not cut a corner even to gain the woman he clearly admires.

13.text: Stay the night, and in the morning, if he will redeem you, good — let him redeem. But if he is not willing to redeem you, then as the LORD lives, I myself will redeem you. Lie down until morning."
13.amp: ...as the LORD lives [chai-YHWH -- a solemn oath], I will redeem you myself. Lie down until the morning.
13.notes: Boaz binds himself by oath in the name of the living LORD to redeem Ruth if the nearer kinsman declines -- her security is now guaranteed by his word sworn before God.

14.text: So she lay at his feet until morning, and rose before anyone could recognize another; for he said, "Let it not be known that the woman came to the threshing floor."
14.notes: Boaz guards Ruth's reputation as carefully as his own -- the night's bold appeal is kept above suspicion. Honor on both sides.

15.text: And he said, "Bring the shawl you are wearing and hold it out." So she held it, and he measured out six measures of barley and laid it on her; then he went into the town.
15.notes: A pledge of intent and provision: Ruth does not go back to Naomi empty-handed, and the heap of grain is a sign that Boaz will not rest until the matter is settled (v.18).

16.text: When she came to her mother-in-law, Naomi asked, "How did it go, my daughter?" And Ruth told her all that the man had done for her.
16.notes: The Hebrew reads, literally, 'Who are you, my daughter?' -- perhaps asking, in effect, 'are you now a betrothed woman or still a widow?' Ruth's answer is the whole night retold.

17.text: And she said, "He gave me these six measures of barley, for he said, 'Do not go back empty-handed to your mother-in-law.'"
17.amp: ...'Do not go empty [reqam -- the very 'empty' Naomi named in 1:21] to your mother-in-law.'
17.notes: reqam (H7387) = empty-handed -- echoing Naomi's lament, 'the LORD has brought me back empty' (1:21). Boaz's gift is a deliberate reversal: the emptiness is being filled.

18.text: Then Naomi said, "Wait, my daughter, until you know how the matter turns out; for the man will not rest unless he settles it this very day."
18.notes: Naomi's counsel is now rest and trust: the redeemer is at work, and his character guarantees the outcome. Ruth's part is to wait while Boaz acts -- a fitting picture of resting in a redeemer's faithfulness.
